biggest_gap.title: p00's own G1 company gate fails on a correct product when the machine is busy: its differential flags the audit log because the log changes while it is being asked
biggest_gap.detail: The full verify at 417f1990 failed on one test: G1CompanyIsolationTests.A_user_of_company_X_cannot_reach_company_Y_through_any_endpoint, which is p00's own gate. It reported company X's read-only user getting different answers from GET /api/audit/log?take=20002 (20002 is one of company Y's values) and from the same request with a value that exists nowhere. On the real product the value cannot matter. The audit log clamps take to 200 (src/Modules/Audit/Erp.Modules.Audit/AuditEndpoints.cs:110), so both requests ask for 200 of 307 rows. The two windows differ by one row at the boundary: the control ends at 06:59:24.659 with a next cursor, and the Y answer goes on to an older row at 06:59:24.638. The gate's second ask of the same pair also differed. So the user's audit log moved during the pair; this is not a company-Y oracle. Run on its own on a quiet machine, the test passed twice (2 min 26 s and 2 min 25 s). In the suite, at a load of 15 to 31 on 16 threads, it took 8 min 30 s and failed. A gate that flags a correct product depending on machine load still counts as a failing test, so the round is blocked. It also matters beyond this round. Every module a UAE trading or manufacturing company needs (sales, purchasing, stock, VAT) writes audit rows and queues jobs, so more lists will move while the gate reads them, and integrations will keep failing at random. The fix must keep the differential strict for real oracles, for example by comparing only rows written before the pair started, or by quiescing the job runner during read batches. A retry, a longer timeout or a skip is not a fix.
biggest_gap.evidence: failure-summary.txt and verify-failed/dotnet-suite.log line 814 (the full message is in verify-failed/trx/suite_net10.0_20261105091834.trx). Load: verify-failed/verify-load-samples, 06:59-07:08Z. Runs alone: rerun/rerun.sh, rerun-1.log, rerun-2.log (toolbox, unplanted copy of 417f1990, filter FullyQualifiedName~G1CompanyIsolationTests). To reproduce: run ./erp verify at 417f1990 while the machine is busy, for example with ./erp up seeding a second stack. The test fails intermittently, so it may take more than one run.

Today the dynamic G2 tests cover the Host and letter-case variants, but not the trailing slash (see gate_gaps).

Tenant binding is robust. A middleware that rewrites the principal's tenant claim from X-Tenant-Id after authorization (plant L17) leaked nothing, because the unit of work is bound to the session's tenant when the session is resolved. A header-chosen tenant at resolution would find no user and fail closed.

The new audit surface (p07) passed my live attack. /api/audit/records/<B id>?type=... answers {items:[]} exactly as it does for a random id. Audit log filters and exports with B's values carry nothing of B's. Password and token hashes are stored as [redacted].
